Efficient Synthesis of 1,2-Bis(alkoxycarbonyl)pyrazol-3-ones from  2,3-
Allenoic Acids, Azodicarboxylates and PPh 3 
Ruizhi L üü üüa, Xin Cheng b, Xingliang Zheng b,c , and Shengming Ma a,b* 
Received (in XXX, XXX) Xth XXXXXXXXX 20XX, Accepted Xth XXXXXXXXX 20XX 
DOI: 10.1039/b000000x 
An efficient cascade reaction of 2,3-allenoic acids with dialkyl 
azodicarboxylate in the presence of PPh 
3 affording 1,2-
bis(alkoxycarbonyl)pyrazol-3-ones in moderate yields has 
been developed. The reaction may proceed via the 
intramolecular Michael addition of the expected 2,3-allenoyl 
hydrazines.  
Pyrazol030ones and derivatives are important structural motif for 
agricultural chemistry and pharmaceutical developme nt (Scheme 
1), 
1,2  which exhibits a wide range of biological properti es as 
herbicides, 3 insecticides, 4 analgestic agents, 5 anti0inflammatory 
agents, 6 and therapeutic agents. 7 They have also been used as 
analytical reagents, 8 and dyes. 9 For these reasons, there are many 
reports dealing with the development of efficient s ynthetic 
methods for pyrazol030ones and derivatives. 10  The most widely 
used method is the cyclocondensation of β0keto alkanoates, 10  α0
cyano esters, 11  β0enamino esters, 12  20alkenoates, 13  or 20
alkynoates 14  respectively with hydrazines. Although some 
progress has been achieved, some of these known pro tocols 
require harsh reaction conditions, multiple steps, or low 
efficiency, thus, development of mild, diverse, and  efficient 
method is still highly desirable. 
 
Scheme 1 
 
“Huisgen zwitterion” formed from the reaction of 
azodicarboxylates with phosphines is an important i ntermediate 
in organic chemistry. 
15  However, the chemistry of Huisgen 
zwitterions has received little attention until ver y recent years. A 
number of interesting reactions involving this zwit terion have 
been explored mainly by groups like Miller, 16  Lee, 17  Nair, 18  
Hughes, 19 Wang, 20  and Shi 21  et al. Recently, we have found that 
the “Huisgen zwitterion” 1 can react with 2,30allenols to give the 
2,30allenoyl hydrazines 2 (Scheme 2, eq 1), which further 
undergo palladium0catalyzed coupling0cyclization re action with 
aryl iodides to afford trans 01,20diazetidines 22 or 2,30dihydro01H0
pyrazoles 23 depend on the substituent at the position 2 of 2,3 0
allenols. 2,30Allenoic acid is an important class o f allene 
derivatives. 24 The acidity and the polarized carbon0carbon double 
bond endow this kind of compounds a quite different reactivity as 
compared with 2.30allenols. In conjunction with our  continuous 
study on the chemistry of functionalized allenes, w e envisioned 
the reaction of 2,30allenoic acids with Huisgen zwi tterion 1 may  
afford 2,30allenoyl hydrazines 3, which may have further 
synthetic utility for the synthesis of heterocyclic  products 
(Scheme 2, eq 2). 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Scheme 2 
 
In our initial attempt, we investigated the reactio n of 2,30
allenoic acid  4a with  diethyl azodicarboxylate 5a  in the presence 
of triphenylphosphine. The corresponding results un der different 
conditions were summarized in Table 1. In THF, howe ver, the 
reaction afforded an unexpected 1,20dihydro03 H0pyrazol030one 
product 6a  in 63% NMR yield, which was fully characterized by  
1H/ 13 C NMR, IR, MS, and HRMS analysis  (entry 1, Table 1). 
This must be formed from the intramolecular conjuga te addition 
of the anticipated 2,30allenoyl hydrazine product 3a . It is obvious 
that the carbonyl group is triggering such a transf ormation. 
However, when the reaction was conducted at room te mperature, 
the NMR yield of 6a  dropped to 50% (entry 2, Table 1). Adding 
more triphenylphosphine and diethyl azodicarboxylat e failed to 
increase the yield (compare entry 3 with entry 1, T able 1), and 
shorting the reaction time to 0.5 h did not get better result (entry 4, 
Table 1). The reaction in dioxane also afforded the  product 6a  in 
63% NMR yield (entry 5, Table 1). More solvent effe cts were 
also examined in this reaction and the desired prod uct 6a  can be 
obtained in moderate to excellent yields (entry 609 , Table 1). 
Finally, the reaction condition (1.2 equiv. of PPh 3 and dialkyl 
azodicarboxylate, CH 2Cl 2, 010 oC 1 h then rt 1 h) was defined as 
the optimal set of conditions for this cyclization reaction (entry 9, 
Table 1).

In conclusion, we have developed a convenient casca de 
reaction of readily available 2,30allenoic acids 26 with dialkyl 
azodicarboxlate in the presence of PPh 3 to afford 1,20dihydro03H0
pyrazol030ones in moderate yields. A possible mechanism for this 
cascade reaction is proposed. Further studies on th e scope and 
synthetic applications of this reaction are being c onducted in our 
laboratory.
